title: Functional Interfaces, Lambdas & invokedynamic
subtitle: Explore Java 8+ functional programming, SAM contracts, method references, and how the JVM uses invokedynamic and LambdaMetafactory to execute lambdas with zero class-file disk overhead.
mentalModel: A Lambda is not syntactic sugar for an anonymous inner class; it is desugared by javac into a synthetic private method and linked dynamically at runtime via invokedynamic and LambdaMetafactory.

failureModes: Effectively Final Variable Mutation: Attempting to modify a local variable from within a lambda body causes a compilation error because lambdas capture the value of the variable, not the stack frame variable itself.
Overusing Lambdas for Complex Multiline Logic: Placing complex 20-line business logic inside lambdas degrades stack trace readability, making debugging difficult compared to named methods.
tradeOffs: Anonymous Inner Class vs Lambda: Anonymous classes create separate .class files and have distinct 'this' scopes. Lambdas have no disk footprint, share the enclosing lexical scope, and are faster to load via invokedynamic.
theoryData.productionScenario: In asynchronous microservices with Spring WebFlux / CompletableFuture, replacing legacy new Runnable() and new Consumer() anonymous classes with lambdas reduced Metaspace class metadata overhead by 35% and improved bootstrap startup latency.

interviewQA.q: Why must local variables referenced inside a lambda expression be final or effectively final?
interviewQA.a: Because local variables reside on the Thread Stack (which is destroyed upon method return), while lambdas can outlive the enclosing method (e.g. executed asynchronously on another thread). Java captures a copy of the variable's value onto the heap; requiring invariance prevents race conditions and value inconsistency between the stack and the heap copy.

interviewQA.q: How does invokedynamic differ from traditional invokevirtual / invokespecial opcodes?
interviewQA.a: Traditional opcodes resolve method dispatch based on static class symbols at compile/link time. invokedynamic decouples the call site from the target method, allowing a user-defined bootstrap method (BootstrapMethod, e.g. LambdaMetafactory) to dynamically determine and link the CallSite at runtime.

quizData.question: Can an interface with 1 abstract method and 3 default methods be marked with @FunctionalInterface?
quizData.answer: Yes! @FunctionalInterface requires exactly one SINGLE ABSTRACT METHOD (SAM). It can contain any number of default or static methods.

quizData.question: Does compiling a Java class containing 5 lambda expressions produce 5 additional .class files on disk?
quizData.answer: No. Unlike anonymous inner classes (which generate OuterClass$1.class, OuterClass$2.class, etc.), lambdas are compiled into synthetic private methods inside the same class and linked at runtime via invokedynamic.
